message.content: The game has concluded. MiMo Stoic has won. I played to maximize my win rate by using Brainstorm to draw into answers and maintaining mana efficiency with fetchlands. Flame of Anor provided valuable removal and card draw when needed. The opponent played aggressively but ran out of resources.

gameOver.message: Player MiMo Stoic is the winner

annotations.description: Fetching a basic Island instead of Tundra is suboptimal here. With Swords to Plowshares in hand, having access to white mana is valuable. Tundra provides both blue and white mana, enabling Daze (as a blue source that can be returned) AND Swords to Plowshares. A basic Island only provides blue. Additionally, with two Wastelands in hand, the player has strong mana denial tools - having their own mana on a dual land that covers both colors is more resilient to their own mana constraints. The downside of Tundra (vulnerability to opponent's Wasteland) is real but relatively minor compared to the upside of having white mana access, especially since they have two Wastelands of their own and can fetch basics later.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched a basic Island from Flooded Strand
annotations.betterLine: Fetch Tundra to have access to both blue mana for Daze/Force of Will and white mana for Swords to Plowshares, maximizing flexibility with the current hand.

annotations.description: Using Force of Will to counter a Daze on a Thundertrap Trainer (a 1/2 creature) is a significant overcommitment of resources. Force of Will costs a card from hand plus 1 life, making it a 2-for-1 against yourself. The Thundertrap Trainer is a low-impact creature - just a 1/2 that cantrips. The opponent only spent a free Daze (returning an Island) to counter it, meaning they invested very little. MiMo Stoic could have simply let the Daze resolve and lost only the Trainer, then replayed it next turn or deployed other threats. Instead, they're down Force of Will plus an exiled blue card (likely Brainstorm or Stern Scolding) to resolve a 1/2 creature. This leaves them without their best counterspell for the rest of the game against whatever threats the opponent presents.
annotations.actionTaken: Used Force of Will (alternative cost: exile a blue card + pay 1 life) to counter Daze targeting Thundertrap Trainer.
annotations.betterLine: Let Daze resolve and counter the Thundertrap Trainer. Replay Trainer next turn when you have more mana to pay for Daze, or hold Force of Will for a more impactful threat from the opponent. Paying 1 life into Daze was also an option since both Islands were tapped, but simply accepting the tempo loss would preserve Force of Will for critical moments.

annotations.description: Using Force of Will (exiling a blue card + 1 life) to counter a Daze protecting a 1/2 Thundertrap Trainer is a massive overcommitment of resources. Force of Will is a 2-for-1 card disadvantage to protect a low-impact creature. MiMo Stoic has a second Thundertrap Trainer in hand and could simply replay it next turn, preserving Force of Will for a much more impactful counterspell battle.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Force of Will using alternative cost (exile blue card + 1 life) to counter Daze and protect Thundertrap Trainer
annotations.betterLine: Let Daze resolve and counter the Thundertrap Trainer. Save Force of Will for a critical spell. Cast the second Thundertrap Trainer next turn when you have mana to pay for Daze if needed, or hold up Stern Scolding as interaction.

annotations.description: MiMo Stoic targeted their own Thundertrap Trainer with Force of Will instead of targeting the opponent's Daze. This results in spending Force of Will (plus exiling a blue card and paying 1 life) to counter their own creature, wasting at least 3 cards (Force of Will, exiled card, and Thundertrap Trainer) for no benefit whatsoever.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted own Thundertrap Trainer with Force of Will, countering their own creature spell
annotations.betterLine: Target Daze with Force of Will to counter it, allowing Thundertrap Trainer to resolve and enter the battlefield

annotations.description: Exiled Thundertrap Trainer (their backup Wizard and creature) instead of the more expendable Stern Scolding for Force of Will's alternative cost. Thundertrap Trainer is a key card that enables Flame of Anor's two-mode selection, and they have two Flame of Anors in hand. Stern Scolding is a narrow, situational counterspell that is the least valuable card to keep.
annotations.actionTaken: Exiled Thundertrap Trainer to pay for Force of Will's alternative cost
annotations.betterLine: Exile Stern Scolding instead - it's the most expendable card in hand. Keeping the second Thundertrap Trainer preserves a backup Wizard for the two Flame of Anors and an additional creature threat.

annotations.description: Over-committed to counter a Thundertrap Trainer (a 1/2 value creature) by using Force of Will and exiling Brainstorm - one of the best cards in Legacy - to protect a Daze. After this exchange, hand is left with Scalding Tarn, 2x Wasteland, Swords to Plowshares, Island - extremely land-heavy with only one spell. Swords to Plowshares could cleanly answer the Trainer if it resolved, and Brainstorm was critical to dig out of a land-heavy hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Force of Will (exiling Brainstorm) to counter opponent's Force of Will, protecting Daze targeting Thundertrap Trainer
annotations.betterLine: Let the opponent's Force of Will resolve (countering Daze), allow Thundertrap Trainer to resolve, and answer it later with Swords to Plowshares while retaining Brainstorm and Force of Will for more impactful threats

annotations.description: Pitching Brainstorm (one of the best cards in Legacy) to Force of Will a Thundertrap Trainer is an overpay. While the opponent also invested their Force of Will, Sonnet Vorthos had Swords to Plowshares to deal with the 1/2 creature body later. The main concern is the ETB trigger finding a spell, but spending Force of Will + Brainstorm to prevent that is expensive when those cards could answer bigger threats.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Force of Will (pitching Brainstorm) to counter opponent's Force of Will, ultimately stopping Thundertrap Trainer via Daze
annotations.betterLine: Let opponent's Force of Will resolve countering Daze, allow Thundertrap Trainer to resolve. Keep Force of Will and Brainstorm for more impactful threats. Use Swords to Plowshares on the Trainer if the body becomes relevant.

annotations.description: With the opponent at only 2 Islands and tapped out after spending Force of Will, this was a prime opportunity for mana denial. Playing Wasteland to destroy one of their Islands would leave them at 1 land with depleted resources, and with a second Wasteland in hand, could potentially lock them out entirely next turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Played basic Island
annotations.betterLine: Play Wasteland, immediately sacrifice it to destroy one of the opponent's Islands, then play the second Wasteland next turn to potentially destroy their remaining land, executing a devastating mana denial strategy while they're resource-depleted.

annotations.description: Playing Scalding Tarn instead of Wasteland misses an opportunity for immediate mana denial against an opponent with only two Islands. Destroying one of their Islands with Wasteland would cut them to one land, creating a massive tempo advantage while the opponent is already down resources (Force of Will and Thundertrap Trainer in graveyard).
annotations.actionTaken: Played Scalding Tarn as land for turn
annotations.betterLine: Play Wasteland and immediately sacrifice it to destroy one of the opponent's two Islands, crippling their mana development. Save Scalding Tarn for a future turn when you need to fetch a specific color (like White for Swords to Plowshares).

annotations.description: Force of Will's flashback cost is {3}{U}{U}, which is extremely difficult to pay with only 2 lands on board. The alternate cost (1 life + exile blue card) cannot be used as a substitute for flashback costs. Stern Scolding's flashback cost of {U} would be immediately available and relevant in Legacy where many key creatures have power/toughness 2 or less.
annotations.actionTaken: Gave Force of Will flashback via Snapcaster Mage
annotations.betterLine: Give Stern Scolding flashback - at {U} it would be castable immediately and provide cheap interaction against opponent's creature threats

annotations.description: Cast Ponder before playing a land. Should play Wasteland first (free land drop), potentially using it to destroy one of the opponent's tapped Islands to cut them to 1 land, then cast Ponder with the Island. Playing land before casting spells is fundamental sequencing - it preserves options and provides more information before committing mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Ponder without first making a land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Wasteland first, then consider destroying one of the opponent's Islands (cutting them to 1 land which is devastating), then cast Ponder with Island, keeping Tundra open for Swords to Plowshares on Snapcaster Mage.

annotations.description: When ordering cards from Ponder, the player put Misty Rainforest on the bottom and Stifle on top. Given their hand of 2x Wasteland and 2x Swords to Plowshares with only 2 lands on board, they desperately need a land drop. Misty Rainforest is a fetchland that would both provide an immediate land drop AND thin the deck. Stifle is a narrow reactive card that doesn't address their current needs - they're behind on board with a Snapcaster Mage threatening them, and they need to develop their mana base to cast their Swords to Plowshares effectively while also deploying Wastelands.
annotations.actionTaken: Put Misty Rainforest on bottom and Stifle on top of library
annotations.betterLine: Put Stifle on bottom and Misty Rainforest on top, drawing the fetchland to make a land drop and fix mana development

annotations.description: Playing Wasteland without immediately using it to destroy one of the opponent's Islands is debatable. The opponent has only 2 Islands (both tapped) and a Snapcaster Mage. Destroying an Island now (or threatening to next turn) could be strong since the opponent is mana-light. However, the bigger question is whether to cast Swords to Plowshares on Snapcaster Mage first (while opponent's lands are tapped) before playing the land. With Tundra untapped and opponent tapped out, this was a window to remove Snapcaster Mage for free without worrying about countermagic. Playing the Wasteland first is fine sequencing-wise since it doesn't use mana, but not casting Swords on the Snapcaster while the opponent is tapped out could be a missed opportunity - though keeping Swords for bigger threats like a future Murktide from the opponent is also reasonable.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Wasteland as land drop
annotations.betterLine: Playing Wasteland is fine, but should strongly consider casting Swords to Plowshares on Snapcaster Mage while opponent is tapped out, then potentially using Wasteland to destroy one of opponent's Islands to keep them mana-constrained.

annotations.description: Sonnet Vorthos passed the turn without taking any action despite having productive options available. The opponent has a Snapcaster Mage (2/1) on board and only two tapped Islands. Sonnet Vorthos could have cast Swords to Plowshares on the Snapcaster Mage (using Tundra for W) to remove the threat and deny future flashback value, or activated Wasteland to destroy one of the opponent's Islands (leaving them with just one land). Both of these lines generate meaningful advantage. Additionally, Phelia is listed in the graveyard so there's nothing to attack with, but passing without using Swords or Wasteland when the opponent is tapped out wastes a clean window to act.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority and skipped to attacks without casting any spells or activating Wasteland, despite having untapped mana and the opponent being tapped out.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Swords to Plowshares targeting Snapcaster Mage while the opponent's Islands are tapped and they can't counter it. This removes a threat and prevents future flashback shenanigans. Could also consider Wastelanding an Island to further constrain their mana.

annotations.description: Sonnet Vorthos has an untapped Wasteland and the opponent has no nonbasic lands (only two basic Islands), so Wasteland activation wouldn't help there. However, the player missed the opportunity to cast Swords to Plowshares on the opponent's Snapcaster Mage. Snapcaster Mage is a 2/1 that can attack and has already provided its ETB value, but removing it prevents 2 damage per turn and denies a potential blocker. More importantly, with the opponent having only 2 Islands tapped, this is a window where they can't counter the Swords (no mana available). Leaving the Snapcaster alive while having two Swords and an untapped Tundra is a missed opportunity to use a removal spell when the opponent is tapped out.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed the turn without taking any action, leaving untapped Tundra and Wasteland unused.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Swords to Plowshares targeting Snapcaster Mage while the opponent's two Islands are tapped, removing the threat for free without risk of counterplay.

annotations.description: Sonnet Vorthos has Snapcaster Mage on the opponent's board and Swords to Plowshares in hand with Tundra untapped to cast it. The Snapcaster Mage is a threat that can attack and has already provided value (giving flashback to a spell in graveyard). More importantly, Sonnet Vorthos could use Wasteland to destroy one of the opponent's Islands, constraining their mana. With the opponent at only 2 Islands, destroying one would significantly limit their ability to cast spells. Swords to Plowshares on Snapcaster before combat prevents 2 damage and removes a body. While passing isn't terrible, using Wasteland on an Island here is free value that constrains the opponent's mana development.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without taking any action during precombat main phase.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Wasteland targeting one of opponent's Islands to constrain their mana to just one land, and/or cast Swords to Plowshares on Snapcaster Mage before it can attack.

annotations.actionTaken: Fetched Volcanic Island from library with Scalding Tarn
annotations.betterLine: Fetch basic Mountain to play around opponent's Wasteland while still having access to {1}{U}{R} for Flame of Anor with the two Islands already in play

Flame of Anor is an instant and could be cast in post-combat main or even on opponent's end step. Casting it precombat taps out MiMo before dealing 2 combat damage, and if the drawn cards include something useful to play, having already tapped out limits options.

annotations.description: Sonnet Vorthos declined to cast Swords to Plowshares on Snapcaster Mage before it attacked, taking 2 damage. While they could cast it after attackers are declared (and still can during the declare blockers step or after damage), the decision to pass priority here without using Swords is not necessarily wrong since they can still respond. However, with Snapcaster Mage having already provided its ETB value (giving Stern Scolding flashback), removing it is reasonable. The real question is whether using Swords on a 2/1 is worth the card when Sonnet Vorthos is at 17 life. Taking 2 damage to save a Swords for a bigger threat is defensible, but Snapcaster is a key creature in the opponent's deck and they have no other board presence. Using Wasteland on Volcanic Island during their combat to deny them red mana could also be considered.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority during combat, allowing Snapcaster Mage to attack unblocked for 2 damage.
annotations.betterLine: This is debatable - saving Swords for a bigger threat like a potential Murktide from the opponent is reasonable. However, activating Wasteland on Volcanic Island to cut off red mana sources could have been considered at end of their turn instead.

annotations.description: Sonnet Vorthos declined to cast Swords to Plowshares on the attacking Snapcaster Mage (which is tapped, indicating it attacked). Snapcaster Mage is a 2/1 that already provided its ETB value (likely flashing back Stern Scolding or similar), and removing it now costs only W mana (Tundra is untapped) while preventing future damage. More importantly, removing Snapcaster Mage puts another instant in the graveyard, which helps fuel Murktide Regent's delve. With 6 cards already in graveyard, removing Snapcaster now and having 7 cards in graveyard (plus lands potentially) makes casting Murktide much easier. The opponent also has Volcanic Island meaning they have red mana for potential burn/removal, so racing is important.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority during combat without using Swords to Plowshares on the tapped Snapcaster Mage.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Swords to Plowshares targeting Snapcaster Mage using Tundra. This removes the threat, adds to graveyard count for Murktide Regent, and the 2 life gained by opponent is negligible compared to the continued damage and board presence of Snapcaster.

annotations.description: Sonnet Vorthos declined to use Wasteland to destroy opponent's Volcanic Island (their only red source) or cast Swords to Plowshares on the tapped Snapcaster Mage. The Snapcaster Mage is a meaningful threat that already provided value (likely flashing back Stern Scolding to counter Phelia based on the graveyard state). More importantly, Swords to Plowshares should be cast on the Snapcaster Mage while it's tapped and the opponent has no untapped mana to protect it - waiting gives the opponent a chance to untap and hold up countermagic. Wasteland on Volcanic Island would also cut off the opponent's red mana, potentially stranding cards in hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without taking any action, ending the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Swords to Plowshares targeting Snapcaster Mage while opponent is tapped out (all lands tapped from casting Snapcaster + using its ability). This removes the threat for free with no counterplay possible. Could also Wasteland the Volcanic Island to cut off red mana.

annotations.description: Sonnet Vorthos cast Murktide Regent before playing a land (Misty Rainforest or Wasteland were available). While Murktide can be cast via Delve using the 6 cards in graveyard (Flooded Strand, Force of Will, Daze, Scalding Tarn, Phelia, Ponder) plus 1 blue mana, playing Misty Rainforest first and cracking it would put another card in the graveyard, potentially allowing Murktide to enter with more +1/+1 counters (one more instant/sorcery exiled). Additionally, casting Murktide before land drop means if it gets countered, they've missed the opportunity to have an extra land in play. Also, casting the creature in precombat main phase rather than waiting gives the opponent more information. However, the bigger issue is sequencing: Wasteland could have been used to destroy the opponent's Volcanic Island before they untap, cutting them off red mana sources, but that should probably happen before committing Murktide into potential countermagic. Playing Misty Rainforest first, fetching an Island, would add a fetchland to graveyard for Delve fuel and provide an additional mana source as backup.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Murktide Regent before playing a land drop for the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play Misty Rainforest first, crack it to fetch an Island (adding another card to graveyard for Delve fuel and potentially getting a bigger Murktide), then cast Murktide Regent. Could also consider using Wasteland on Volcanic Island first to cut opponent off red mana before committing the win condition.

annotations.description: Sonnet Vorthos has two Wastelands and the opponent has Volcanic Island and Prismatic Vista as nonbasic lands. Activating Wasteland to destroy Volcanic Island during MiMo's postcombat main (after they've presumably tapped out or used their mana) would deny them their only red source and constrain their mana. With Murktide Regent in hand needing to be cast soon, keeping tempo pressure on the opponent's mana is important. However, Sonnet Vorthos also needs lands to cast Murktide Regent (which costs 7 minus delve), so sacrificing a Wasteland reduces their own mana. With 9 cards in graveyard, Murktide could potentially be cast for UU with enough delve fuel, so losing a land to Wasteland might be acceptable. The decision is debatable but passing up the opportunity to cut off the opponent's red mana (their only Volcanic Island) when you have two Wastelands available is worth questioning.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate either Wasteland, passing priority.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Wasteland targeting Volcanic Island to cut off MiMo's red mana source, since you have a second Wasteland and enough lands/graveyard cards to still cast Murktide Regent next turn.

annotations.description: Murktide Regent is on the stack and Sonnet Vorthos has Force of Will in hand (with no blue cards to exile for alternative cost, but could hard-cast it with 5 mana available: Island, Tundra, Tundra, Wasteland, Wasteland = only 4 colored mana sources plus Wastelands for colorless = UUWCC which isn't enough for 3UU). Actually, looking more carefully: Island (U), Tundra (U/W), Tundra (U/W), Wasteland (C), Wasteland (C) = at best UUUCC or UUWCC, which doesn't cast Force of Will (3UU needs 5 mana with 2 blue). They have UUWCC = 5 mana but only 2-3 blue. Force of Will costs 3UU = they need UU + 3 generic = UU + UWC or UU + WCC. With Island+Tundra for UU and Tundra+Wasteland+Wasteland for WCC = yes, they CAN hard-cast Force of Will for 3UU! Murktide Regent is a massive flying threat (likely 8/8+ with delve exiling instants/sorceries from graveyard). Instead of countering it with Force of Will, they played Flooded Strand, allowing Murktide to resolve. This is a game-losing mistake - Murktide Regent with multiple +1/+1 counters is extremely difficult to deal with, especially when the opponent has counter backup.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Flooded Strand from hand instead of countering Murktide Regent on the stack.
annotations.betterLine: Hard-cast Force of Will (3UU) using Island + 2x Tundra + 2x Wasteland to counter Murktide Regent, which is a must-answer threat.

annotations.description: Sonnet Vorthos declined to use Wasteland to destroy one of MiMo Stoic's nonbasic lands (Volcanic Island or Prismatic Vista). MiMo Stoic has Volcanic Island as their only red source, and destroying it would cut them off red mana entirely, potentially preventing Flame of Anor or other red spells. However, Sonnet Vorthos may be holding Wastelands to use at a more impactful moment, and they need lands to cast Murktide Regent. The opponent has 5 lands including only one nonbasic worth targeting (Volcanic Island), so using Wasteland on Volcanic Island to deny red mana seems reasonable, especially since Sonnet Vorthos has 6 lands and Murktide can be cast cheaply with Delve (9 cards in graveyard means it could cost as little as UU).
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate either Wasteland, passing through precombat main without action.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Wasteland targeting Volcanic Island to cut MiMo Stoic off red mana. With 9 cards in graveyard, Murktide Regent can still be cast with the remaining lands (exile 5 cards from graveyard to pay for the generic costs, pay UU from remaining lands).

annotations.description: Opponent has two Wastelands on the battlefield threatening to destroy Prismatic Vista for free card disadvantage. Cracking Prismatic Vista now to get a Wasteland-proof basic land is virtually free and protects against a clear on-board threat.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without activating Prismatic Vista or taking any action.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Prismatic Vista to fetch a basic Island or Plains, converting a vulnerable nonbasic land into a Wasteland-proof basic before the opponent can destroy it for free.

annotations.description: Fetched a basic Plains instead of a Tundra. With Murktide Regent in hand needing blue mana, and two Wastelands on their own board only producing colorless, having another blue source via Tundra would provide more flexibility. The reasoning even mentions wanting a basic Island but chose Plains instead.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched Plains from Flooded Strand
annotations.betterLine: Fetch Tundra for the flexibility of producing either {W} or {U}, maximizing blue sources for Force of Will and Murktide Regent. Alternatively, if wanting a basic for Wasteland protection, a basic Island would have been more aligned with the blue-heavy hand.

annotations.description: MiMo Stoic passed with Flame of Anor available that could draw 2 cards (the only useful mode with no creatures or artifacts on board). The opponent has 2 Wastelands that threaten Volcanic Island, which is MiMo's only red source. If Volcanic Island gets destroyed, Flame of Anor becomes uncastable. Drawing 2 cards in this board stall would provide significant card advantage.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without taking any action in precombat main phase
annotations.betterLine: Activate Prismatic Vista to fetch a basic Island (protecting mana base against Wasteland), then cast Flame of Anor choosing 'draw two cards' to generate card advantage while red mana is still available

annotations.description: Sonnet Vorthos has two Wastelands and the opponent has Volcanic Island and Prismatic Vista as nonbasic lands. Using Wasteland to destroy Volcanic Island would cut the opponent off red mana (relevant for Flame of Anor and other red spells) and reduce their mana development. With 6 lands in play and only needing to cast Murktide Regent (which uses Delve) and holding Force of Will plus Swords to Plowshares, sacrificing a Wasteland would still leave adequate mana. Declining to use Wasteland when there's no downside to mana-denying the opponent is a missed opportunity.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate either Wasteland, passing through the main phase.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Wasteland targeting Volcanic Island to cut the opponent off red mana, constraining their ability to cast multicolored spells like Flame of Anor.

annotations.description: Sonnet Vorthos declined to activate either Wasteland to destroy one of MiMo Stoic's nonbasic lands (Volcanic Island or Prismatic Vista). With the opponent at 5 lands including two nonbasics, destroying Volcanic Island would cut off their red mana source entirely, which is relevant for cards like Flame of Anor. Wasteland is a tempo tool that should be used proactively, especially when the player is behind on life (13 vs 20) and struggling to resolve threats. The player appeared to be frustrated with not being able to cast Murktide Regent and passed without using available resources.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate either Wasteland, passing without taking any action.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Wasteland targeting Volcanic Island to cut off MiMo Stoic's only red mana source, constraining their future plays and reducing their mana development while the information is available.

annotations.description: Cast Flame of Anor during own main phase instead of activating Prismatic Vista first to thin the deck before drawing 2 cards. Additionally, as an instant, Flame of Anor could be cast at end of opponent's turn to preserve information and flexibility. The main concrete mistake is not fetching first before drawing.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Flame of Anor immediately during main phase to draw 2 cards without fetching first
annotations.betterLine: Activate Prismatic Vista first to thin the deck, then either cast Flame of Anor now or wait until end of opponent's turn to cast it, preserving flexibility

annotations.description: MiMo Stoic chose Sonnet Vorthos as the target for Flame of Anor's 'draw two cards' mode, giving the opponent two free cards instead of drawing them themselves. With no creatures or artifacts on the battlefield, the draw mode was the only useful option, and it should have targeted themselves.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Sonnet Vorthos (opponent) to draw two cards from Flame of Anor
annotations.betterLine: Target yourself (MiMo Stoic) to draw two cards, gaining crucial card advantage in this resource-depleted game state
